acceptance: A run through MCP with seed=N writes a bundle whose config seed is N, and the same seed through the CLI yields the same recorded query parameters.
A run with iterations=K records K measurement iterations; omitting both arguments gives the same bundle configuration as the CLI defaults.
Invalid values are rejected with a validation error before any work starts, and remote mode bounds iterations under the existing admission policy.
The response states the effective seed and iterations.
The MCP reference parameter table and the CLI-to-MCP omission list are updated, doc contracts are regenerated, scripts/verify_mcp_conformance.py passes, and a changelog.d fragment is present.
context:
Origin: adversarial review of an agent-facing strategy for BenchBox, 2026-11-12. Owner decisions quoted here were made on that date. Line numbers are hints; re-read the cited file before relying on them.

Evidence: the run_benchmark signature has twelve parameters and no seed or iterations; a search of the tool module finds neither word.

Decision gate (before coding): confirm how the shared runner receives seed and iterations from the CLI and reuse that path; if MCP would need a second code path to set them, stop and report. Check whether this touches a soundness path that needs the external reviewer, and say so in the PR.

Verification rubric: pass only if the CLI-against-MCP equivalence is shown with real bundles from both entry points, at scale 0.01 on a local platform.

Related: mcp-start-benchmark-nonstandard-scale-note-20261111 is an existing gap between the two run tools; keep the two tools aligned here.

Guardrails: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. Related items are delivered together on one feature branch and one PR, as their umbrella item names (site work: BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site); squash-merged. Add a changelog.d fragment for any user-facing change. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers) runs only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy (make comment-policy-check). Stop and report instead of widening scope; scope removed during review must be re-homed to a named item or dropped by the owner with a reason.

Review note (2026-11-12): while in this code, record in the PR what the run_benchmark response already says about validation. If it carries no integrity verdict, do not add one here; record it with the tracker's defer tool on this item so the owner can promote or dismiss it.

Revision (2026-11-13), after an independent critique and owner decisions: the dependency on the prompt fix is removed; both ship on the umbrella's branch.
description:
Problem: the CLI run command accepts --seed and --iterations, but MCP run_benchmark has neither, so a run made through MCP cannot be repeated exactly or given more measurement iterations.

Owner decision (2026-11-12): expose seed and iterations only, keep the CLI defaults, and report the effective values in the response. Validation mode and tuning stay CLI-only.

Outcome: run_benchmark and the durable start_benchmark accept seed and iterations with the same meaning and defaults as the CLI.

Non-goals: validation mode, tuning, and any change to the platform-option allow-list.
